sections.overview: This deep-sea notacanthid fish is known from the Atlantic, including the Mediterranean.
sections.identification: It has an elongated, eel-like body, a small mouth and a long row of short dorsal spines. One Mediterranean specimen was described as light grey with darker margins around the gill cover and mouth.
sections.habitat: It lives near the seabed on deep continental slopes, with records from roughly five hundred to nearly three thousand metres; limits vary among compilations.
sections.diet: Available accounts describe it as an epibenthic feeder on small bottom-dwelling invertebrates, including worms and crustaceans.
sections.behavior: Its deep-water lifestyle is difficult to observe directly, and species-specific behavior is sparsely documented.
sections.reproduction: The sources consulted provide little species-specific information on its reproduction.
sections.ecology: It is one of several deep-water spiny eels in the family Notacanthidae. A study of the Levant Basin reported a specimen at about one thousand four hundred metres.
sections.conservation: The sources consulted do not provide a current global conservation category or population trend for this species.
